result.summary:
The edge result is proved on both slices (t = 3 with y = √3, and t = 3 with y = 3/2), but only for sectors j ≤ 12. It uses exact algebra plus rigorous interval arithmetic. Let x* be the unique real root of P2(x, y, √3) in [-3, 1]. Then on [-3, r_next) the twist is the floor of every sector j ≤ 12 iff x ≤ x*. Here r_next is the next real zero of det(B_{4,0} - lambda_4 I), and it is a root of P1. The whole script runs in about 25 s.

How it is proved:
- **Blocks.** The slice blocks are built exactly in sympy. The exact determinant matches the srepr polynomial exactly (3^9 D = P), and factor_list gives P = -16384·P1·P2.
- **Roots.** The real roots of P1 and P2 are isolated with rational endpoints, using the norm over Q(√3) and exact sign tests. Both norms are squarefree, so every root is simple.
- **Transversality.** Interval enclosures show dP2/dx ≠ 0 and P1 ≠ 0 on x* ± 1e-6.
- **Sign of m.** Interval Cholesky shows B_{4,0} - lambda_4 is positive definite at x = -3. Then the eigen-branch argument (Rellich) gives m > 0 on [-3, x*), m(x*) = 0, and m < 0 on (x*, r_next).
- **Other blocks.** Interval Cholesky on covers of [-3, x* + 0.02] certifies all 116 other non-twist blocks per slice, using the Alefeld-Mayer theorem.

Not proved:
- Sectors j > 12 near the edge. The large-j proof covers only x in [-3, -1.5].
- The gauge-orthogonal edge.
- That the closed-form blocks are the charge blocks of H + GG*. This WP relies on earlier numerical checks for that and does not re-derive it.

The .md file also lists what a 2-D (t, y) region would need. That part is a plan, not proved: no root collisions in x (discriminant and resultant nonzero, leading x-coefficient nonzero), one positive-definite base point per connected region, a 3-D interval cover near the edge surface, and certificates for the middle sectors 12 < j < 80.

That the closed-form blocks equal the H+GG* charge blocks rests on earlier numerical validation, not on an independent symbolic proof in this WP.

claims.topic: (1) Nielsen-Olesen instability: primary source
claims.claim: Nielsen and Olesen (1978) showed that a charged vector (Yang-Mills) field in a uniform external magnetic field has an unstable mode. This is the original source of the chromomagnetic instability.
claims.title: An Unstable Yang-Mills Field Mode
claims.doi_or_url: https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(78)90377-2 (bibliographic record and abstract read from the INSPIRE API: https://inspirehep.net/api/literature?q=title%20%22An%20unstable%20Yang-Mills%20field%20mode%22)
claims.quote: It is shown that there exists an unstable mode of the field.
claims.relevance: This is the physical prototype for the twist: one spin-aligned, lowest-Landau-level mode whose eigenvalue drops below zero. The Elsevier full text did not load (it redirects), so only the abstract was read. Nothing in it concerns compact or Berger geometry.

claims.topic: (1) Savvidy vacuum
claims.claim: Savvidy (1977) found that one-loop radiative corrections make the perturbative Yang-Mills vacuum unstable, which favours a constant chromomagnetic field.
claims.title: Infrared Instability of the Vacuum State of Gauge Theories and Asymptotic Freedom
claims.doi_or_url: https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(77)90759-6 (record and abstract read from the INSPIRE API)
claims.quote: The radiative corrections to the Yang-Mills massless theory are found to lead to an instability of the vacuum state.
claims.relevance: Background only. This is a one-loop effective-potential result, not a classical Hessian floor theorem.

claims.topic: (1) Lowest Landau level and gyromagnetic ratio 2 mechanism
claims.claim: For a charged W boson with S3 = eps in {-1,0,1} in a constant field B, the spectrum is E^2 = (2n1+1)gB + 2 eps gB + mW^2. The non-minimal coupling gives gyromagnetic factor 2, so the Zeeman term is twice the first Landau-level term and the ground state sits at -gB + mW^2. In pure Yang-Mills this ground state is tachyonic for every B != 0, which is the Nielsen-Olesen instability.
claims.title: Vortex Zero Modes, Large Flux Limit and Ambjorn-Nielsen-Olesen Magnetic Instabilities
claims.authors: Stefano Bolognesi, Chandrasekhar Chatterjee, Sven Bjarke Gudnason, Kenichi Konishi
claims.quote: Note that the non-minimal coupling of the W boson is responsible for the anomalous gyromagnetic factor gs = 2. Now the Zeeman term is twice the first Landau level term, and so the ground state energy is En,-1 = -gB + m2W ... For pure Yang-Mills (i.e. mW = 0) the ground state is always tachyonic for any B != 0. This is the instability discussed by Nielsen, Olesen and
claims.relevance: This is the textbook statement of the mechanism behind our twist, a Landau term plus a g=2 Zeeman term. I extracted the quote myself with pdftotext from the arXiv PDF, so the wording is verbatim (PDF line breaks removed). It is a flat-space formula. That our closed-form twist eigenvalue lambda = (x+(j+2)/sqrt t)^2 + 2 sqrt t x - y^2 is the Berger-sphere analogue of a Landau-plus-Zeeman energy is my CONJECTURE, not something this source says.

claims.topic: (1) Nielsen-Olesen instability, later usage
claims.claim: In later physics usage, Nielsen-Olesen unstable modes are exponentially growing soft modes of non-Abelian gauge-field fluctuations around a colour-magnetic background.
claims.title: Schwinger mechanism enhanced by the Nielsen--Olesen instability
claims.quote: exponentially growing unstable modes
claims.relevance: Secondary confirmation of the mechanism. Not directly relevant to compact or homogeneous geometry.

claims.topic: (1)+(4) Chromomagnetic backgrounds on S^3: closest physics prior art
claims.claim: Avramidi and Collopy study static, covariantly constant SU(2) gauge fields on the round S^3 in S^1 x S^3 Yang-Mills theory. Their stated result is that only the background containing purely spinor (fundamental) SU(2) representations is stable, and every other covariantly constant background has negative modes.
claims.title: Thermal Yang-Mills Theory In the Einstein Universe
claims.quote: the only configuration of the covariantly constant Yang-Mills background that is stable ... all other configurations contain negative modes and are unstable
claims.relevance: This is the closest prior art I found: negative modes of homogeneous chromomagnetic backgrounds on S^3. It covers only the round sphere and covariantly constant fields. Nothing in the abstract treats a Berger squashing t, a two-parameter (x,y) circle-symmetric family, or a polynomial wall where the floor changes. Only the abstract was read, and the quote is as returned by WebFetch's extraction model.

claims.topic: (3)+(4) Yang-Mills on S^3 with symmetric (SO(4)-invariant) ansatz
claims.claim: Kumar, Lechtenfeld and Picanco Costa test the linear stability of SO(4)-invariant, time-dependent SU(2) Yang-Mills solutions in conformally flat (closed FLRW) spacetimes. They find all such cosmic Yang-Mills backgrounds linearly unstable.
claims.title: Instability of cosmic Yang-Mills fields
claims.authors: Kaushlendra Kumar, Olaf Lechtenfeld, Gabriel Picanco Costa
claims.quote: all cosmic Yang-Mills backgrounds are rendered linearly unstable
claims.relevance: This paper uses the round S^3 (SO(4) symmetry) and Floquet analysis of a time-dependent background. In what I read it is not a squashed-sphere Hessian floor computation, and I found no paper by this group on squashed S^3. It is useful as a citation for symmetric-ansatz fluctuation analysis on S^3.

claims.topic: (4) Homogeneous SU(2) Yang-Mills on Bianchi IX (SU(2)-group) spacetimes
claims.claim: Jin and Maeda study Einstein-Yang-Mills dynamics in class A Bianchi spacetimes, including Bianchi IX, and report late-time chaos and an unstable Kasner circle.
claims.title: Chaos of Yang-Mills Field in Class A Bianchi Spacetimes
claims.quote: the Kasner solution is not an attractor
claims.relevance: Bianchi IX spatial slices are left-invariant metrics on SU(2), which include Berger spheres. A homogeneous (left-invariant) SU(2) gauge ansatz like our m_i is standard in that literature. I learned about the ansatz from a search snippet and the abstract does not state it, so only the dynamics claim is verified. This line of work studies dynamics, not the second-variation floor.

claims.topic: (2) Bochner-Weitzenbock formula for the Yang-Mills second variation
claims.claim: Bourguignon-Lawson's Bochner-Weitzenbock formulas give the covariant Hodge Laplacian on bundle-valued 1-forms as rough Laplacian + Ric + a curvature (F) term. On 2-forms the extra term is Ric^Id + 2R^M. These formulas feed the Yang-Mills Jacobi operator.
claims.title: Nonexistence of weakly stable Yang-Mills fields (secondary source restating Bourguignon-Lawson as its Theorem 2.1)
claims.quote: Δ∇ϕ = ∇∗∇ + ϕ∘Ric + ℜg∇(ϕ) ... Δ∇ψ = ∇∗∇ + ψ∘(Ric∧Id + 2RM) + ℜg∇(ψ)
claims.relevance: This is the standard tool behind our H + GG* splitting. On 1-forms, H + d_A d_A* equals the covariant Hodge Laplacian, which by Weitzenbock is nabla*nabla + Ric + an F-term. The Ric + 2F form the task mentions is this. The quote is a secondary restatement, as returned by WebFetch. I could not open the Bourguignon-Lawson original: Springer, Project Euclid and scispace all failed or redirected to login. Cite the original by its record (next item), and check the printed formula and theorem number against the paper before citing.

claims.topic: (2) Bourguignon-Lawson 1981: bibliographic record
claims.claim: Bourguignon and Lawson (1981) is the standard reference for stability and gap phenomena of Yang-Mills fields over spheres and locally homogeneous spaces.
claims.title: Stability and isolation phenomena for Yang-Mills fields
claims.authors: Jean-Pierre Bourguignon, H. Blaine Lawson, Jr.
claims.quote: Stability and isolation phenomena for Yang-Mills fields (zbMATH keywords: "weakly stable Yang-Mills fields", "self-dual", "gap phenomena")
claims.relevance: This verifies the citation only. zbMATH has no review text and the full text was not accessible. I did not verify any theorem number or page.

claims.topic: (2) Stability on spheres (Simons / Bourguignon-Lawson)
claims.claim: Per nLab, every weakly stable Yang-Mills connection on S^n with n >= 5 is flat (Simons, announced in 1977 without written publication, proved in Bourguignon-Lawson 1981). On S^4, weakly stable SU(2), SU(3) or U(2) fields are self-dual or anti-self-dual.
claims.title: stable Yang-Mills connection (nLab entry)
claims.quote: Every weakly stable Yang-Mills connection on S^n for n≥5 is flat.
claims.relevance: Background on spheres: S^3 is not covered by the n >= 5 theorem. Han-Wen (arXiv:2601.17649) paraphrase Bourguignon-Lawson as having proved there 'is nontrivial weakly stable' connections on S^n for n >= 5. That contradicts nLab and is probably a misstatement, so do not quote Han-Wen on this point.

claims.topic: (2) Nonexistence near the round metric
claims.claim: Han and Wen prove that for every metric in a C^2-neighbourhood of the round metric on S^n (n >= 5) there are no nontrivial weakly stable Yang-Mills connections.
claims.title: Nonexistence of weakly stable Yang-Mills fields
claims.quote: there is no nontrivial weakly stable Yang-Mills connections for any metric
claims.relevance: A perturbation-of-metric stability result, comparable in spirit to varying the Berger parameter t. It applies to n >= 5, not to S^3.

claims.topic: (2) Homogeneous / symmetric spaces: Laquer and Kobayashi-Ohnita-Takeuchi
claims.claim: Laquer (1984) studied the stability of the Yang-Mills functional near canonical connections and classified the symmetric spaces that admit unstable Yang-Mills fields. Kobayashi-Ohnita-Takeuchi (1986) showed that all Yang-Mills connections on P^2(Cay) and E6/F4 are unstable.
claims.title: Laquer, 'Stability properties of the Yang-Mills functional near the canonical connection'; Kobayashi-Ohnita-Takeuchi, 'On instability of Yang-Mills connections' (content via the Han-Wen restatement)
claims.authors: H. Turner Laquer; S. Kobayashi, Y. Ohnita, M. Takeuchi
claims.doi_or_url: https://doi.org/10.1307/mmj/1029003019 ; https://eudml.org/doc/173776 ; content quote from https://arxiv.org/html/2601.17649v1
claims.quote: extended this program by classifying symmetric manifolds admitting unstable Yang-Mills fields
claims.relevance: The bibliographic data comes from the zbMATH and EuDML records I opened. The descriptions of the results are secondary (Han-Wen) and I did not read the originals. Laquer's index computation for the canonical connection on a compact group such as SU(2) = S^3 with the round metric is the nearest classical 'Hessian of an invariant connection on a group' computation. The canonical connection on SU(2) is a particular left-invariant connection, which in our family would be some (x,y) at t=1; which point that is, I have not checked.

claims.topic: (2) Morse index on round spheres
claims.claim: Lei Ni gives a multiplicity estimate for the Jacobi operator of a nonflat Yang-Mills field over S^m, refining Simons' stability result.
claims.title: A multiplicity estimate for the Jacobi operator of a nonflat Yang-Mills field over S^m
claims.quote: The result also implies the earlier Morse index estimates for both cases.
claims.relevance: These are index bounds on round spheres. They give no floor-location or wall result.

claims.topic: (3) Laplace spectrum of Berger spheres
claims.claim: Lauret gives an explicit formula for the smallest nonzero Laplace eigenvalue of every homogeneous metric on S^3 and describes the full spectra of 3-dimensional Berger spheres.
claims.title: The smallest Laplace eigenvalue of homogeneous 3-spheres
claims.quote: For the subfamily of 3-dimensional Berger spheres, we obtain a full description of their spectra.
claims.relevance: This is the scalar Laplacian. It is citable for the representation-theoretic (Peter-Weyl, charge-sector) method on Berger spheres that our block decomposition also uses. It is not the gauge Hessian.

claims.topic: (3) Hodge Laplacian on 1-forms of Berger spheres
claims.claim: Henkel and Lauret compute the full spectrum of the Hodge Laplacian on 1-forms for the canonical variation (Berger 3-spheres) and prove an explicit formula for the first eigenvalue of general homogeneous metrics on S^3.
claims.title: Hodge Laplacian on 1-forms of homogeneous 3-spheres
claims.quote: the first explicit computation of the full spectrum of the Hodge-Laplacian for a canonical variation
claims.relevance: This is the most relevant spectral prior art. At the trivial connection (x=y=0), H + GG* on su(2)-valued 1-forms reduces to three copies of the Hodge Laplacian on 1-forms. That is a standard identity, not taken from this paper, and should be checked against our Blocks class at x=y=0. Their Berger 1-form spectrum should then match our blocks at x=y=0, which gives an independent check. Their paper treats the flat connection only. The abstract also says the formal proof of one result was found by an AI model.

claims.topic: (3) Dirac spectrum on Berger spheres (Bar)
claims.claim: Bar computes Dirac eigenvalues on S^3 and its quotients with Berger metrics, using formulas for the Dirac operator on reductive homogeneous spaces together with Frobenius reciprocity.
claims.title: The Dirac operator on homogeneous spaces and its spectrum on 3-dimensional lens spaces
claims.year: 1992 (Potsdam publication list; the MaRDI/zbMATH record dates it 1993)
claims.venue: Arch. Math. 59 (1992) 65-79 (volume and pages from the Potsdam list); zbMATH 0786.53030
claims.quote: the author calculates the eigenvalues of the Dirac operator on the sphere
claims.relevance: This is a method precedent: Frobenius reciprocity on Berger S^3 is the same structure as our charge-q block decomposition. The quote comes from the zbMATH review (by S. Giambrone) shown on MaRDI, not from the paper.

claims.topic: (3) Dirac spectrum on homogeneous 3-spheres (Kling-Schueth)
claims.claim: Kling and Schueth compute and use the smallest eigenvalue of D^2 for left-invariant metrics on S^3 with positive scalar curvature, and show that Dirac-isospectral left-invariant metrics are isometric.
claims.title: On the Dirac spectrum of homogeneous 3-spheres
claims.venue: J. Geom. Anal. 32 (2022), no. 11, Paper No. 175
claims.quote: we compute and use the smallest eigenvalue of D²
claims.relevance: This is the closest analogue of our task, the smallest eigenvalue of a first-order-squared operator on homogeneous S^3, found by representation theory. It concerns the Dirac operator, not the gauge Hessian, and no wall or polynomial edge appears in the abstract.

claims.topic: (5) Rigorous positive-definiteness certificate via floating-point Cholesky
claims.claim: Rump gives a rigorous, rounding-error-aware sufficient criterion for positive definiteness of symmetric/Hermitian matrices, including interval matrices, based on one floating-point Cholesky decomposition, plus a criterion to verify non-positive-definiteness.
claims.title: Verification of positive definiteness
claims.quote: We present a computational, simple and fast sufficient criterion to verify positive definiteness of a symmetric or Hermitian matrix. ... It is based on a floating-point Cholesky decomposition and improves a known result.
claims.relevance: This is a directly citable tool for certifying H + GG* - lambda_twist*I > 0 on the non-twist complement of each block, or block - c*I > 0 over interval boxes in D. The quote is verbatim, extracted with pdftotext from the author's PDF. A shifted Cholesky with interval entries can replace Gershgorin near the edge.

claims.topic: (5) Verified bounds for all eigenpairs of Hermitian (and interval) matrices
claims.claim: Rump and Lange give verification methods with mathematically certain bounds for all eigenvalues and eigenvectors of Hermitian matrices, clusters included. The methods apply to interval data, with bounds that hold for every matrix in the interval.
claims.title: Fast computation of error bounds for all eigenpairs of a Hermitian and all singular pairs of a rectangular matrix with emphasis on eigen- and singular value clusters
claims.year: 2023 (as given by the search result; I did not confirm the published venue)
claims.venue: preprint PDF on the author's site (published journal not verified this session)
claims.quote: The computed bounds do contain the true result with mathematical certainty, and the algorithms apply to interval data as well. In that case the computed bounds are true for every real/complex matrix within the tolerances.
claims.relevance: Citable for interval-box eigenvalue enclosure of our blocks of at most 9 states. The quote is verbatim via pdftotext.

claims.topic: (5) Brauer ovals of Cassini and sharper Gershgorin-type sets
claims.claim: For weakly irreducible matrices, the spectrum lies in Brualdi lemniscate sets, which lie in the union of Brauer ovals of Cassini, which lies in the union of Gershgorin disks (sigma(A) in B(A) in K(A) in G(A)). The minimal Gershgorin set lies in B(A).
claims.title: Gersgorin-type eigenvalue inclusion theorems and their sharpness
claims.quote: we investigate the relationships between G(A), the union of Gersgorin disks, K(A), the union of Brauer ovals of Cassini, and B(A), the union of Brualdi lemniscate sets
claims.relevance: Citable improvements over plain Gershgorin for the large-j tail. They might lower the l ~ 640 that plain Gershgorin needs near the edge. Whether they help with our tridiagonal-like rows is untested. The quote is verbatim via pdftotext. Varga's 2004 Springer book 'Gersgorin and His Circles' covers weighted and minimal Gershgorin sets, but I did not open it (Springer login redirect).

claims.topic: (5) Schur complement inertia (Haynsworth)
claims.claim: For Hermitian H partitioned with H11 nonsingular, In(H) = In(H11) + In(H/H11), where H/H11 = H22 - H12* H11^-1 H12.
claims.title: Determination of the inertia of a partitioned Hermitian matrix
claims.relevance: This makes the twist-versus-rest split rigorous. If the complement block minus lambda_twist is certified positive definite, the Schur complement gives the inertia of the full shifted block. The formula comes from Wikipedia, not the paper, so cite the paper by record.

claims.claim: Terao, Watanabe and Ozaki give verified bounds for singular values of structured matrices, aimed at computer-assisted proofs for differential equations, including a lower bound for the minimum singular value that works well on sparse matrices.
claims.title: Verified error bounds for the singular values of structured matrices with applications to computer-assisted proofs for differential equations
claims.authors: Takeshi Terao, Yoshitaka Watanabe, Katsuhisa Ozaki
claims.quote: The method for estimating a lower bound of the minimum singular value is particularly effective for sparse matrices.

result.prior_art_assessment:
Method: every claim above comes from a source opened this session with WebFetch. The quotes from Bolognesi et al., Rump 2006, Rump-Lange and Varga I extracted myself from the PDFs with pdftotext, so those are verbatim. The other quotes are verbatim only as far as WebFetch's extraction model returned them; check them against the source before they go into a paper.

(1) Chromomagnetic instability. The Nielsen-Olesen (1978) and Savvidy (1977) records were fetched. The lowest-Landau-level plus g=2 Zeeman mechanism is stated explicitly in Bolognesi-Chatterjee-Gudnason-Konishi (JHEP 2014): E^2 = (2n+1)gB + 2 eps gB, with the ground state tachyonic for any B != 0 in pure Yang-Mills. The structural match with our twist (unique maximal-charge state, a squared kinetic term plus a linear-in-x 'Zeeman-like' term) is a natural physical interpretation, but it is my CONJECTURE and none of these sources states it. On S^3, the closest physics prior art is Avramidi-Collopy (2012). They find negative modes in every covariantly constant SU(2) background on the round S^3 except the purely spinor-representation one. Squashing, our (x,y) family and any floor-switching wall are absent from the abstract.

(2) Second variation. The Bourguignon-Lawson Weitzenbock formula (rough Laplacian + Ric + curvature term on 1-forms; Ric^Id + 2R^M on 2-forms) is verified only through Han-Wen's 2026 restatement. The original text was not accessible, so theorem numbers and the exact Ric + 2F form must be checked against the paper. The stability literature (Simons; Bourguignon-Lawson; Laquer 1984; Kobayashi-Ohnita-Takeuchi 1986; Han-Wen 2026; Ni 2022) concerns existence or nonexistence of stable Yang-Mills connections and index bounds, mostly on round spheres of dimension >= 4 or 5 and on symmetric spaces. None of what I read computes the Hessian floor along a non-critical, two-parameter family of left-invariant gauge fields on a Berger sphere. Our fields are generally not Yang-Mills critical points, so these stability theorems do not apply directly. Laquer's canonical-connection index computation could overlap our t=1 slice. It is unverified and worth getting.

(3) Berger spectra. Strong, citable method precedents use Peter-Weyl / Frobenius reciprocity sector decompositions on Berger S^3. Bar did this for Dirac; Lauret (BLMS 2019) gives the full Laplace spectra of Berger spheres; Kling-Schueth (JGA 2022) give the smallest D^2 eigenvalue on homogeneous S^3; Henkel-Lauret (arXiv May 2026) give the full Hodge 1-form spectrum of Berger 3-spheres. Henkel-Lauret yields a concrete independent check. At x=y=0, H + GG* should reduce to three copies of the 1-form Hodge Laplacian (a standard identity, not from their paper), so their Berger spectrum should match our blocks there. I found no Yang-Mills Hessian computation on squashed or Berger S^3 by Kumar-Lechtenfeld-Picanco Costa or anyone else. Their 2021 paper is SO(4)-invariant, round, time-dependent and uses Floquet theory.

(4) Equivariant / homogeneous fields. Homogeneous SU(2) gauge ansatze on SU(2)-group (Bianchi IX) slices appear in Einstein-Yang-Mills cosmology (Jin-Maeda 2005, dynamics only). I found no classification or Hessian floor study of circle-symmetric left-invariant connections on Berger spheres.

(5) Tools to cite. Rump (BIT 2006) verifies positive definiteness through floating-point Cholesky, valid for interval matrices. Rump-Lange give verified enclosures for all eigenpairs, including interval data. Haynsworth (1968) gives inertia additivity across the Schur complement, which makes 'twist versus complement' rigorous. Varga (ETNA 2001) shows Brauer-Cassini and Brualdi sets are nested inside the Gershgorin union, which may cut the l ~ 640 that plain Gershgorin needs near the edge (untested).

Is the edge known? I searched for the Yang-Mills Hessian on Berger or squashed S^3, Morse index of left-invariant connections, chromomagnetic instability on S^3 via the Hopf fibration, and invariant Yang-Mills connections on squashed S^3. I found NO source containing a result of our form: the lowest eigenvalue of the Yang-Mills Hessian (or H + GG*) in a circle-symmetric family switching between a maximal-charge state and a competitor block across a polynomial wall in (x, y, sqrt t). As far as this search reaches, the edge theorem appears new. The search was limited, though. Several classical full texts (Bourguignon-Lawson, Laquer, van Baal's S^3 papers, Hitchin) could not be read, and they are where an overlap at the round point t=1 would most likely sit. Those should be checked before any novelty claim is made.

result.summary:
I drafted the three WP4 pre-registrations. No test was run, and no edge, floor or spectrum was computed at any held-out point. The only things computed were structural design checks and the draw of the held-out points.

Two of those checks change what the hypotheses can claim:

1. **Her region in x is bounded on both sides, so it is not a half-line.** Her value λ₀ grows like x². The state θ⁰⊗τ₀ in sector 0 is gauge-orthogonal for every (x, y, t), and its Rayleigh quotient is affine in x. So for every (y, t) she stops being the floor at large |x|, under both the H+GG* and the gauge-orthogonal definitions. The same argument works in the SU(3) family through θ⁸⊗X₈. This means H1's "half-line", the sentence's "by more than", and H3(3)'s "half-space" must all become "interval". Every earlier scan stopped at x = −3, which is why the region looked like a half-line.

2. **The (x, y) ansatz is general up to constant gauge.** It covers every left-invariant, circle-symmetric SU(2) field on (t, 1, 1), for any circle weight k. So "random fields beyond the ansatz" do not exist inside that class. Prereg B is therefore split: B-I checks that the class behaves as its reduction (a code control that can only fail on a code error), and B-II tests H2's kill criteria at random points over a much wider box than before.

**What each pre-registration contains:**
- **A (held-out points):** 48 fixed points never computed before. The prediction is that the edge is the largest real root of P₂ in [−3, 3], with competitor (4, 0), to 1e-9. It is measured by an independent full-spectrum code path. Further arms: the competitor class at small y; no undercut from sectors 13–60; one interval with no holes. Controls: three code gates, a negative control using P₁, and the proved lower bound.
- **B:** described in point 2 above.
- **C (SU(3)):** metric 2b with the fibre field x freed. D3 found the U(2)-invariant fields are exactly 4-dimensional (u, x, y, z), with z removable by gauge. Fixed before the run: her x² coefficient is exactly 3/4 (her fibre charge √3/2), and her region is bounded. Predictions from the sentence: she is the floor somewhere (weak and strict versions), her region lies mainly on the side where the field turns against her charge, it is one interval, and the competitor is nearly blind to x (and neutral where u, y ≥ 1). Controls K1–K5 include an SU(2) known-answer check and the Test 2b Maurer–Cartan point.

Pre-registration should be committed before any of these tests runs; I did not commit (hard rule).

Commutant dimensions: 1 for k=±2, 3 for k=0 and k=±1. Reductions: (x,y,z)->(x,sqrt(y²+z²)); k=-1 (x,y) -> (-x,y); k=0 -> y=0.

The large-j half (j>=80) is unaffected. I deliberately did not compute x_lo; prereg A, arm A4, measures it.
H1, H3(3) and the sentence in she-is-the-law need rewording from half-line/half-space to interval [x_lo, x*]. That is a correction to existing docs, and I did not edit them (hard rule).

Prereg B leaves circle-invariant fields that are not left-invariant (sector-mixing) undesigned: no builder exists for them and no non-automatic prediction is available. It also leaves non-constant gauge lifts out of scope. The SU(2)_L x U(1)_R isometry description of (t,1,1) is standard and was not re-proved here.

Prereg C's x² coefficient 3/4 and the boundedness argument are hand derivations, gated by C-quad and C-lin at run time. In SU(3) 'her own circle' (lambda8, the stretched fibre) differs from her charge circle (H = diag(1,0,-1)); the prereg fixes x as the lambda8 component and records the ambiguity.
Runtime of prereg C is not measured (sector matrices up to 1728x1728, about 20x65 x-points x 9 sectors); the prereg requires a one-point timing first.

If H is the YM Hessian, then H + d_A d_A* = Delta_A + R^nabla, not the Hodge Laplacian Delta_A. The two agree only at a flat connection, such as x=y=0. Overall: all 22 cited sources exist. The quotes are verbatim or faithful, checked against the arXiv API, INSPIRE, zbMATH, Crossref, author PDFs (my own pdftotext) and nLab. Metadata fixes: KOT pages are 165-189. Ni is Geom. Dedicata 217 (2023) 92, DOI 10.1007/s10711-023-00817-8. Rump-Lange is J. Comput. Appl. Math. 434 (2023) 115332, DOI 10.1016/j.cam.2023.115332. Bar is 1992. Lauret's DOI is 10.1112/blms.12213.

Substantive error (math, not bibliography): the item (2) assessment says H + d_A d_A* equals the covariant Hodge Laplacian, i.e. nabla*nabla + Ric + an F-term. Han-Wen (following BL81 (6.14)) write the second variation as S = Delta^nabla + R^nabla, so the Jacobi operator is nabla*nabla + Ric + 2R^nabla. So H + d_A d_A* = Delta_A + R^nabla. That is the Hodge Laplacian plus one more curvature term, and it equals the Hodge Laplacian only at flat connections (x=y=0). The 'Ric + 2F' form belongs to the Jacobi operator, not to the Weitzenbock identity. In the 2-form Weitzenbock formula the '2' multiplies the Riemann tensor, not F. Fix this before writing up the H + GG* splitting.

Missing prior art that bears directly on S^3:
(a) M. Stern, 'Geometry of minimal energy Yang-Mills connections', J. Differential Geom. 86 (2010) 163-188, DOI 10.4310/jdg/1299766686. I verified the Crossref abstract: 'We prove related results ... for 3-dimensional manifolds of nonnegative Ricci curvature.' The zbMATH review: for a complete 3-manifold with Ric>=0 and a stable YM connection, the curvature is parallel and lies in a flat subbundle, and 'F_A=0 unless M has local flat factors'. X. Jin (arXiv:2609.24045, 2026, verified) states 'Stern's argument implies that stable Yang-Mills connections on the round three-sphere are flat.' Berger spheres near t=1 have positive Ricci, so this is the nearest stability theorem for critical points on the squashed S^3 too. It covers critical points only.
(b) Han-Wen's summary of Laquer 1984 lists 'compact simple Lie groups' among the compact symmetric spaces that do not admit weakly stable YM connections. That includes SU(2)=S^3 at t=1. This is secondary and unverified in Laquer, but it is a likely overlap at the round point, and the assessment does not mention it.
(c) Possibly relevant, verified abstracts only: Jin 2026 (arXiv:2609.24045) gives a quantitative upper bound on the lowest Hessian eigenvalue for non-stable abelian YMH critical points on the round S^3, which is a floor-type estimate. Han-Wen 2026 (arXiv:2602.15666) gives pinching conditions under which weakly stable YM connections are flat; Berger spheres near round are pinched, but the dimension range of delta(n) was not checked.

The novelty conclusion ('edge theorem appears new') is suitably hedged. It stands as far as I searched: one targeted search found no Hessian-floor computation for left-invariant connections on Berger S^3. It should still be stated only after Laquer, BL81 (Project Euclid may be free), Stern 2010 and van Baal's S^3 work are read in full. The physics interpretation (Landau + g=2 Zeeman) is correctly labelled conjecture. The Savvidy claim's phrase 'favours a constant chromomagnetic field' is not in the fetched abstract.

reproduced: D1 (the ansatz is general up to constant gauge) holds within its stated scope. I re-read the sympy commutant for the condition L M - k M L = 0 (dimensions 1/3/3/3/1 for k = -2..2), the explicit gauge maps and the code in scripts/edge_wp4_design_checks.py. The ansatz diag(x,y,y) commutes with L for k = +1. Rotating z away gives rho >= 0. k = -1 maps to (-x, y) by a pi rotation about e1. k = 0 and |k| = 2 reduce to y = 0. Receipt: wp4_design_checks.json.

The prereg-A section 2 argument (her region is bounded below) is correct. In sector 0 the state theta^0 (x) tau_0 is index 0 of T2.hessian_and_gauge. I measured |G* e0| = 0 at x in {-3, 0.5, 2}, and H_00 has zero second difference in x (it is the constant 18.88 at y=1.2, t=4). COMPUTED, my check /tmp/wp4rev/chk2.py. That state has charge 0, so it is orthogonal to both twist copies, and the A-bound gate direction (x_lo >= r_lo) is right.

P2 is literally a factor of the numerator of det(B_{4,0} - lambda_4) (scripts/ricci_su2_edge_polynomial.py), and P1 is the other factor of that same determinant. edge_polynomial.txt lists their degrees as (5,6,12) and (7,8,16), and I read the 61-term count for the (5,6,12) factor there. I did not re-check the 113-term count for P2.

Risk to the running certificate, checked at points that are not held out (COMPUTED, j <= 12, /tmp/wp4rev/chk3.py). Over an 11x15 (y,t) grid of D's range, min phi_A at x in {-3,-1.5} is 2.35. On a 3x3 grid, min phi_S at those x is 2.69. The largest closed-form bound r_lo over the grid is -7.33. phi_A first turns >= 0 at x of about -4.1 at (y=3, t=3), -5.6 at (0.5, 3), -6.3 at (3, 10), -7.5 at (0.5, 10) and -5.75 at (1.5, 6), each with a single sign change on [-40, -1.5]. So at these grid points the lower edge does not cut into D. This is a grid check, not a proof. The closest margin is at y=3, t=3, about 1.1 below x=-3.
refuted_or_wrong: FATAL measurement bug in prereg A section 5. In the full H+GG* sector spectrum, lambda_j has multiplicity 2, not 1, because the q=-(l+2) mirror block has the same value. COMPUTED: the multiplicity is 2 for j=0..4 at (x,y,t) = (-2,1.5,4) and (-1,0.7,6), in both the full and the slice spectra. Over x in [-40,1], t in {3,5,10}, y in {0.5,1.5,3}, j <= 12, min(mirror - lambda) = -6.8e-13. EE.phi_S already removes two copies for this reason. Prereg A takes out only one eigenvalue near lambda_j, which makes phi_full <= 0 identically and equal to 0 up to roundoff inside her region. The '>= 0 to < 0' sign-change scan and the brentq refinement then act on noise, so the A1 and A4 measurements are meaningless as written. Fix: require exactly 2 eigenvalues within tolerance at a point away from the crossing, remove both, and stop otherwise.

Prereg B, gate B-half, is wrong by the proved lower edge. 'Exactly one sign change of phi_A on [x*-3, x*]' fails whenever x_lo > x*-3. That is a real lower edge, not a hole, and it would be wrongly scored against H1's no-hole clause. x_lo is already about -4.1 at (y=3, t=3), and B-II draws rho up to 6 and t down to 0.5. Fix: scan [r_lo(rho,t), x*] and require exactly two sign changes (lower edge going up, upper edge going down).

Prereg A, gate table versus verdict rule: the A4 gate requires x_lo > -40, but section 7 says an interval reaching -40 is not a failure. Pick one. Also, A-bound computes r_lo in closed form. If r_lo > -40 at every point (the largest r_lo over D's grid is -7.33), the clause 'x_lo inside the scan' passes automatically and should be dropped, so A4's only content is 'no holes'.

Labelling is inconsistent. Prereg C section 2 is headed 'PROVED by the argument' for F1 (x^2 coefficient 3/4) and F2, but the report labels F1 CONJECTURE (a hand derivation, not machine-checked). Under hard rule 4 these must be CONJECTURE until C-quad and C-lin pass. My own reading: the 3/4 = |ad(X8)E_theta|^2 derivation is right if the M_8 components are taken in the orthonormal coframe (e_8 = X8/sqrt t). The prereg should state that convention explicitly, because the coefficient picks up a factor of t otherwise.
overclaims: A1 is presented as 'the edge equation predicted at held-out points'. But P2 is a factor of det(B_{4,0} - lambda_4) built from the same closed-form rows that A-code-1 checks against the full spectrum. So agreement to 1e-9 follows automatically once the competitor is (4,0) and the edge is the largest root of P2 in [-3,3]. The only content that can fail is (a) the competitor identity, (b) the root selection, and (c) the edge not lying in [-3,3]. The prereg should say this, and A-ctrl-neg (P1 is the other factor of the same determinant) should be described as a branch-selection check, not a negative control. 'Held-out' adds little here, because nothing was fitted.

B-II 'tests H2 across the class', but the x and k of each draw are discarded: edges are located on x in [-10,10] for each (rho,t). B-II is therefore a 200-point random (y,t) scan of the reduced family, not evidence about general fields. B-I is a pure code control, which the prereg already admits.

B-N is restricted to rho >= 1.1 after (N) was seen to fail at y = 0.5. That narrows the hypothesis after the fact. It is acceptable only if H2's text is amended to the same domain and the threshold 1.1 is justified, not tuned. The B-S threshold of 0.5 was likewise chosen after seeing the ratios 0.16, 0.064 and 0.165 (from twist_anatomy, as quoted in prereg B), so it is a loose post-hoc bar.

'Every sector' at held-out points rests on j <= 12, plus A3 checking j in [13,60] at one x only (x* - 0.02). j = 61..79 is never checked. The j >= 80 interval proof covers only D, and most held-out points lie outside D (t from 2.2, y up to 3.2, x up to x*). B-II has no high-j check at all, even though rho goes up to 6 and |x| up to 10.

C-P2 (midpoint side) is nearly fixed by structure: her region lies inside [r_lo, r_hi], the roots of lambda_b - <v,Hv>, whose midpoint is the vertex of a parabola with x^2 coefficient 3/4 and a linear coefficient computable before the run. C-sigma is also fixed by hand from the lambda8-weight (p+2q)/sqrt3. Passing C-P2 is therefore weak evidence for 'turns against her charge' unless it is compared with what the bounding parabola already forces.
result.notes:
The preregs can be committed only after these fixes; with one of them, prereg A's measurement is not usable at all. Everything below is my review, with checks run in /tmp/wp4rev (nothing written to the repo, single process, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1).

Must fix before commit:
(1) Prereg A section 5 removes one copy of lambda_j, but lambda_j has multiplicity 2 in the full spectrum (CONFIRMED, COMPUTED). Remove both copies, and gate that exactly 2 eigenvalues lie within tolerance at a point away from the crossing.
(2) Prereg C has the same risk. In the self-conjugate sectors (0,0), (1,1) and (2,2), b and its conjugate may share the sector, giving multiplicity 2. I did not check this for SU(3), so it is PLAUSIBLE, not confirmed. Make the number of copies removed a measured gate, not an assumption. Note that Test 2's classify_point compares lam_b <= mu[0] + tol and so does not have this problem; phi_S as defined in prereg C does.
(3) Rewrite B-half as described above (scan [r_lo, x*], require two sign changes).
(4) Make the A4 gate and the A4 verdict agree, and drop 'x_lo > -40', which A-bound makes automatic.
(5) Add a minimum number of scored points to B-II, for example a set count of draws with an edge in range and rho >= 1.1; below it, report 'inconclusive'. As written, 'no edge in range' points are simply not scored, so B-II could pass with almost no data.

Forking paths to close:
- B-S does not say which twist slope is used. It should be her lambda in the competitor's sector.
- B-sym and B-I fit the charge operator from the field but leave the fitting procedure unspecified. Name it (for example T2.fit_signs) and give its tolerance.
- C's extension of the x scan stops at [-32,32] with step 1. Instead, scan to the closed-form [r_lo, r_hi] for each shape point and add an analogue of A-bound to C (x_lo >= r_lo and x_hi <= r_hi). A also lacks the x* <= r_hi gate.
- The step-0.25 grid in C, and the step-0.01 grid in A4, cannot see holes narrower than one step. State that limit.
- C-P1 strict failure is pre-excused as a 'weak negative' that 'may permit'. Decide now whether it counts against.
- A-code-3 says 'vanishes to 1e-8 relative' without saying relative to what. A suitable normalisation is the sum of the absolute values of the terms.
- Small point: D1 says '|k| >= 3 cannot match'. Half-integer k, which arises if the circle is taken in SU(2) with period 4pi, should be mentioned too. It also gives only the weight-0 match, so the y = 0 ansatz, and the conclusion stands.

On the question 'is the ansatz general up to gauge': yes, for left-invariant fields, constant gauge lifts and the right circle about e0. The scope list in the prereg is honest. The isometry group SU(2)_L x U(1)_R (t != 1) is assumed, not re-proved.

Certificate risk: the open issue in the report is real but, at the grid points I checked, not realised. Min phi_A at x in {-3,-1.5} over D's (y,t) grid is 2.35 (COMPUTED). The smallest margin found is at y=3, t=3, where x_lo is about -4.1. That is grid evidence, not proof. The background certificate will settle it.

Disclosure: I evaluated phi_A and phi_S at points in D's (y,t) range. None of them is a held-out point, so prereg A's held-out points remain uncomputed.

result.summary: WP1 is done, and it found a problem with the earlier edge results. With sectors j ≤ 12, the H+GG* edge over t∈[2,12], y∈[0.25,3] (an 11×12 grid) is set by eight blocks, counted up to the q↔−q mirror: (4,0), (3,½), (2,1), (1,½), (1,3/2), (2,2), (12,6) and (12,7). Each block's det(B−λ_j) numerator was derived exactly (DomainMatrix over the field its entries need) and factored over Q. All 132 grid edges are roots of the right factor, with |root−edge| ≤ 2.4e-13. The (4,0) edge factor is exactly P2 from the earlier edge_polynomial.txt. Six of the eight blocks belong to two near-top families, q=l+1 and q=l; I derived both determinants with j as a symbol. Each family's leading coefficient in l has x=0 as its only root in the edge range, and both coefficients vanish identically at t=2. Numerically, these families undercut the twist in sectors beyond j=12, with their per-sector edges falling toward 0 roughly like 1/j. So every positive j≤12 edge (t≳7, which includes the positive values in exact_edge.json and the exact-edge doc) comes from cutting off at j=12. I confirmed this with the independent non-block builder for both H+GG* and the gauge-orthogonal (slice) spectrum. Conjecture: for 2<t≤12 the all-sector edge is min(x*_12, 0). At t=2, small y, the edge sits lower still, at a negative large-j limit (j=2000 gives −0.6847 at y=0.25). The write-up is research/edge-theorem-20261121/wp1_competitor_map.md.

results.claim: Competitor map, j<=12, H+GG*, 11 t x 12 y grid: eight distinct competitor blocks up to q sign: (4,0), (3,1/2), (2,1), (1,1/2), (1,3/2), (2,2), (12,6), (12,7). (4,0) wins at 77 points (mostly y in [1,~2.5]); (2,1) for y<=0.5, t>=3; (3,1/2) for y~0.75, t<=6; (1,1/2) and (1,3/2) for y~0.75-1, t>=7; (1,3/2) and (2,2) at large y, small t. The (12,6) and (12,7) entries sit in the top allowed sector, so they come from the j<=12 cutoff.

Their leading coefficients in l are c+ = -128 s x (s-1)(s+1)(s^2-2) and c0 = -65536 s x (s-1)(s+1)(s^2-2)(3s^2-4)(sx-2s^2+2)(sx-s^2+2). Both vanish identically at t=2.
